svg.text: K2b Turning station KH: T turns, the Wender holds, the anchor post takes the torque
A ring coil heats, a canned hub turns pots (T) or spins jug blades (S); fixed tools hang on the rim and lean on one post.
ring coil 2.5 kW (boost 3.0), outer Ø 280, inner Ø 135
T: 30 Nm, 0–600 rpm · S: 1.5 Nm, 0–6000 rpm · both through welded thimbles
3 load cells: 10 kg ± 2 g · anchor post Ø 25 takes up to 30 Nm
pocket Ø 125 × 60, gasketed into the glass like a downdraft nozzle
SECTION through KH (pot turning under a hung scraper)
T plug (ware, magnets in a can)
reaction torque goes into the post, not into the Wender: the Wender is free while T stirs, kneads, mills

g.text: KH cells 3.214 kg — every transfer weighed twice (gain on KH, loss in the jaws)
KH cells 3.506 kg (+292 g milk poured about the lip)

svg.text: FROM ABOVE: T turns the pot, the hung tool stands still
kneading roller-and-scraper on a rim bridge;
its arm rests in the post's fork
polar work: θ of T + X of the Wender
reach every point of a Ø 300 disc
FOOD MILL (M3): skins stay on the disc
potatoes boiled in their skins; T 30 rpm, 800 g in 90 s

g.text: 1/4 T turns the pot through the canned hub: a magnet ring outside the welded pocket drives the T plug; nothing is sealed
2/4 Fixed tools hang on the rim and lean on the anchor post: kneading roller, scraper, mill blade — the Wender is free meanwhile
3/4 Food mill: the wedge blade, held by the post, forces boiled potatoes through the 2.5 mm disc; the skins stay on top
4/4 Dicing: the bought dicing kit sits still in its chimney bowl; T drives its slicing disc; the jaws feed onions with the pusher cup
